summary: Pia Guerrini Bione was an Indologist. She earned her Dr.phil. while studying at the Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa and its Classe di Lettere e Filosofia from 1903 to 1907.

Pier Gabriele Goidanich was a linguist who studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore and the University of Milan under Graziadio Isaia Ascoli. He served as professor at the University of Pisa and later at the University of Bologna from 1906 to 1938.

Piero Martinetti was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied under Giovanni Flechia at the University of Turin and at the University of Leipzig, later teaching at Turin, the Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano (1906–1931), and the University of Milan.
Pierre Arènes worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under André Bareau and held an attested post at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique from 2003 to 2004.

Pierre Bourdieu was a philosopher and scholar who studied under Émile Benveniste. He held posts at the Faculty of Arts of Paris, Lille University of Science and Technology, the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences, and the Collège de France (1981–2001).

Pierre Chantraine was a linguist who studied under Alfred Ernout, Antoine Meillet, Joseph Vendryes, and Theodor Bloch. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1928–1969), the Sorbonne (1938–1969), and the University of Paris.
Pierre Charles Olloba d'Ochoa worked in Indology. In 1839, he studied under Garcin de Tassy at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales.

Pierre Dupont worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Sylvain Lévi, Alfred Foucher, Charles Picard, and Moritz Abraham Stern. His career included posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, the Sorbonne, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Pierre Fabricius specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Heinrich Zimmer, Walther Schubring, Sylvain Lévi, Alfred Foucher, and Louis Renou, and later served as a professor at the Royal University of Phnom Penh (1965–1974).

Pierre Fallon was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at KU Leuven and the University of Calcutta. He taught at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, and served as Professor of French Literature at Calcutta from ~1956 to 1980.

Pierre Herman Leonard Eggermont was an Indologist and historian. He earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University, later working as a scientific research associate at the University of Amsterdam (1966–1979) and as a professor at KU Leuven (1969–1984).

Pierre Johanns worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. Educated at KU Leuven and Oxford, he taught philosophy at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, and St. Mary's College, Kurseong, later teaching Sanskrit at the University of Namur (~1939–1951).

Pierre Meile was a linguist and Indologist who studied in France and India under Sylvain Lévi, Alfred Foucher, Émile Benveniste, and others. He served as a professor at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales from 1939 to 1963.

Pierre Rolland was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Karl Hoffmann, Louis Renou, and Armand Minard at Paris, Aix-Marseille, Göttingen, Tübingen, and Erlangen-Nuremberg. In 1969, he was appointed a researcher at the National Centre for Scientific Research.

Pierre-Amédée Jaubert was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He directed INALCO (~1838–1847) and held a professorship in Persian at the Collège de France (1838–1847).
Pierre-Gustave Garrez was an Indologist. He received his education at the Lycée Henri-IV and the Lycée Louis-le-Grand.

Pierre-Philippe Giraudeau was a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at the Séminaire des Missions Étrangères de Paris (~1875–1878) and served as a missionary with the Paris Foreign Missions Society from 1877.

Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Louis Renou. He worked with the École française d'Extrême-Orient, held the Chair of Sanskrit at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1967–2004), and taught at the EHESS.
Pieter Cornelis Verhagen is a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics. He earned his Ph.D. from Leiden University and served as a research fellow there in 1996.

Pieter Hendrik Pott specialized in Tibetology, Indology, and archaeology. He earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University under Frederik David Kan Bosch, later serving as curator at the National Museum of Ethnology and professor of museology at Leiden (1973–1983).
